questions.q: What problem do Level of Detail (LOD) expressions solve?
options: They let a calculation compute at a grain different from the view's own level of detail, which regular aggregation can't do
They make charts render faster by pre-aggregating all data
They replace the need for calculated fields entirely
They only work with date fields, for time-series analysis
questions.explain: A regular aggregation is stuck at the view's grain. LOD expressions let a calculated field declare its own grain — coarser, finer, or unrelated to what's on the shelves.

questions.q: What are the three parts of every LOD expression's syntax?
options: Curly braces, a scope keyword with dimension(s), and an aggregation
A table name, a column name, and a WHERE clause
A dimension, a measure, and a filter
A function name, parentheses, and a default value
questions.explain: The shape is always { SCOPE [dimension] : AGGREGATE([measure]) } — curly braces, the FIXED/INCLUDE/EXCLUDE scope, and the aggregation.

questions.q: Which LOD keyword computes at exactly the dimension(s) listed, ignoring the view's other dimensions and most filters?
options: FIXED
INCLUDE
EXCLUDE
AUTO
questions.explain: FIXED computes at exactly the scope you name, independent of the view — that's what makes it powerful (and why filter order matters, covered in Lesson 71).

questions.q: In { FIXED [Customer Name] : SUM([Sales]) } placed on a view grained by Order ID, what happens to the calculated value across multiple orders from the same customer?
options: It repeats the same customer-level total for every order from that customer
It resets to zero for each new order
It only shows a value for the customer's first order
It errors, because FIXED can't be used with Order ID on the view
questions.explain: FIXED locks the grain to Customer Name regardless of what else is on the view, so every row for that customer shows the same fixed total — exactly what the lab in this lesson has you observe.

questions.q: How does an LOD expression relate to a table calculation, at a high level?
options: An LOD expression computes before most filtering and the view's aggregation; a table calculation computes after the view's query already returns
They are two names for the exact same feature
Table calculations always run before LOD expressions
LOD expressions can only be used inside table calculations
questions.explain: LOD expressions change when in the query pipeline a value is computed — earlier than the view's own aggregation — while table calculations work only with the already-aggregated data on screen. Lesson 72 covers this contrast in depth.
